label: diffuse original-phase unit, weakly tied to input 2/l after digits or q/g
explanation: Active on about 1% of steps. 83% of activation mass falls in the original phase (never at t=0, rare at <DEL>). Within that phase it is diffuse: rate peaks at t=1-2 and again at late positions (orig_idx 7-8). Input token 2 has the biggest lift (9x, 36% of mass); l, 0 and 1 are weaker. The rate also climbs with the number of digits in the sequence and when q/g/2 appeared earlier, e.g. as first_tok or prev2_tok. Even the best predicate tried (input 2 or l after some digit/q/g) reaches only dev F1 about 0.27, and broader predicates trade precision for recall without a coherent rule. It probably reflects accumulated hidden-state content rather than a token-level condition. The copy phase holds 17% of mass, scattered. I did not check what drives magnitude beyond the observation that input 2 covers more of the top quartile.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by phase (input phase: 2, l, 0, 1; copy phase: a, k, m, v; delimiter step: ) and the previous input (most: 2, l, 1, q, x, g; least: o, e, k, -); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=8, L=7 & t=10, L=8 & t=7.
